newsitem.title: USA: Judge ousts Hill & Knowlton from Fla. tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Judge ousts Hill & Knowlton from Fla. tobacco suit.

text.p: The public relations firm Hill & Knowlton will no longer face potential liability in Florida's $1 billion Medicaid suit against the tobacco industry, a state judge ruled Tuesday.
Judge Harold Cohen said the company's actions took place too far in the past for it to be considered a partner in the conspiracy to misinform the public alleged by Florida in its suit.
The judge pointed out that Florida's racketeering statute was not passed until 1977, nine years after Hill & Knowlton ceased providing any public relations support to the tobacco industry.
"Nothing was done by Hill & Knowlton beyond 1968," Cohen said in making his ruling.

However, the judge kept Hill & Knowlton in the case so that if he wishes to enjoin tobacco companies or the public relations firm from continuing in the alleged conspiracy, he will have the power to do so.
After the ruling, Hill & Knowlton attorney Barton Sacher said, "We are ecstatic with the ruling and thank the judge."
